topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic covers the lecture opening, introducing the speaker, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Mutations, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational drivers of cancer, evaluating the interplay between intrinsic genetic errors, inherited risks, and environmental factors highlighted by epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms by which biological agents cause cancer, focusing on viral and bacterial drivers and the classic case of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical pathways through which direct and indirect mutagens, such as radiation and chemical compounds, damage DNA and cause mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic factors in cancer development, including chronic inflammation, the two-stage initiation-promotion model, and developmental timing.

topics.label: Methods for Determining Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and bacterial methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.
